## Description

A ciliate of 20–50 µm (~32 µm) of marine and brackish waters that forms red tides. It hunts
cryptophytes and retains their chloroplasts (and their nucleus) for weeks: it photosynthesises with
them, but as it cannot replace them they wear out and it has to eat again. It moves in very fast jumps
with its cirri. An equatorial groove where the cirri arise makes the cell look two-part.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: not seeded in the default drops (inoculate it from the Catalogue).
<!-- /GENERATED -->

[Kleptoplasts](../../mechanics/symbioses.md) taken from *Cryptomonas* (really marine cryptophytes such as
*Teleaulax*) that decay; [jumps](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md#jumps); the groove is a body notch.
Kleptoplast half-life, load and jump speed are orders of magnitude.

## Not implemented yet

- The stolen nucleus that keeps the plastids active is not modelled.
- Prey is the freshwater *Cryptomonas*, not *Teleaulax*.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Kleptoplasty is unique to it; shares photosymbionts with *P. bursaria* and jumps with *Halteria*.
